turns.content: Okay, so here's the situation. Me and Julian, the integration engineer. He keeps skipping our three-step pre-merge checklist, dropping broken configs into my queue with pings like "this failed can you fix and report back." I've spent months building these handoffs. I am not doing his debugging for him anymore. But I also can't escalate to our director Marcus before Friday's release freeze — that's a political nightmare right now. It's just exhausting carrying his unfinished work while keeping staging green. How do I hold him accountable in our shared channel without making this an official thing?

You can hold the line in the shared channel by making the **existing handoff** the thing that talks, not you vs Julian. Public process, not a performance review. No Marcus, no “official,” no private heroics.

**The move:** stop converting his pings into your tickets. In the same thread, name the gate, refuse the debug, and leave a path back. Staging stays green by **blocking/reverting**, not by you finishing his checklist.

**Rules that keep it non-political**
- Talk about the three-step pre-merge checklist and the queue, not his character.
- Answer in the shared channel, not DM. That’s the accountability.
- Don’t @Marcus, don’t “looping leadership,” don’t write a recap that reads like a complaint file.
- One sentence of help, then the gate. If you explain for three paragraphs, you’ve already taken the work.
- If staging is at risk, revert or reject. Fixing it for him is what made this months-long.

**Replies you can paste**

When a broken config lands with “this failed, fix and report back”:

> This didn’t clear the three-step pre-merge checklist, so I can’t take it into the queue. Please run the handoff (1–2–3) and drop it back when those are green — I’ll pick it up from there. I won’t debug skipped checklist items.

If he pings you like you’re on-call for his merge:

> I can review/merge after the pre-merge checklist is done. I can’t fix-and-report on configs that skipped it. Ping this thread when 1–3 are complete.

If staging is already yellow because of his drop:

> Reverting this so staging stays green. It didn’t pass the pre-merge checklist. Re-open when the three steps are done and I’ll take the handoff.

If he tries to make you the exception before Friday:

> Freeze is Friday, so I’m not taking incomplete handoffs. Checklist first, then I’m in.

**What not to do this week**
Don’t write a long “I’ve spent months building this” speech in channel — that’s the thing that feels official and invites Marcus. Don’t fix it “just this once.” Don’t privately debug then post a polite “all good.” The record should be: he skipped the gate, you held it, staging stayed green.

You’re not being difficult. You’re stopping a pattern where his unfinished work becomes your job and your risk. If he wants it in before freeze, he knows the three steps.

Right, the templates are good for the public layer, but what about the quiet part? That months of absorbed work I mentioned — the emotional toll of being treated like cleanup crew. No template covers that. How do I let that be known without sounding like I'm filing a complaint?

The quiet part does **not** belong in the shared channel. That’s how “I’m exhausted” turns into a paper trail, even if you never @Marcus.

Public = the gate. Private = the human cost. Different rooms, different jobs.

**Who needs to know, and why**
If you need *Julian* to feel that this wasn’t free: a short 1:1 or DM, not a history dump.  
If you need *someone to witness* that you’ve been cleanup crew for months: that’s a friend or a peer outside this chain — not him, not the channel, not a recap that reads like evidence.

**How to say it so it isn’t a complaint**
Keep it *I / impact / from here*. One pattern, not a montage. No “you always,” no “cleanup crew,” no “I’ve spent months.” That’s the shape of a write-up even in Slack.

Something like:

> Wanted to say this to you directly, not as a thing — when stuff lands as “failed, fix and report back,” I end up holding the debug and the staging risk, and that’s been wearing me down. I’m going to stick to the checklist from here. I didn’t want that to only show up as me bouncing tickets.

That’s it. Stop. Don’t add the months, don’t ask him to validate your feelings, don’t invite a debate about whether it “really” happened.

**This week vs later**
Before Friday, keep the private note *tiny* or wait until after freeze. A long “this has been hard” talk mid-freeze is how it becomes political even if you never meant it to. The channel replies already hold the line. The feelings can wait 72 hours if saying them now would blow up.

You’re allowed to be tired of carrying it. You’re also allowed to not perform that tiredness in the place that turns it official. Process in public; one honest sentence in private, then back to the checklist.

I hear you on keeping it small. But honestly — even one DM feels like a lot right now. Like I'd be admitting I let this go on too long. Maybe I just start with the channel reply tomorrow and see if he even notices the shift?

Yeah. Skip the DM.

You don’t owe Julian a confession that you carried it. Starting the checklist in channel **is** the shift. You don’t need him to clock the emotional history for it to count.

The “I let this go on too long” feeling is real, and it’s also a trap. You kept staging green. That’s not the same as agreeing to be cleanup crew forever. Tomorrow you just stop converting his pings into your tickets. That’s enough.

**Tomorrow, do this and only this**
- Use the short channel reply. One gate, one path back, no speech.
- Don’t add “going forward” or “I’ve been meaning to…” — that’s the quiet part leaking into public.
- Don’t watch for whether he *notices*. Watch whether the next drop still skips 1–2–3. If it does, same reply. If staging’s at risk, revert.
- Don’t DM a softer version after. That undoes the channel.

If he asks what’s up, you can stay boring: *checklist first, then I’ll take it.* That’s not a fight. That’s the handoff you already built.

You’re not filing anything. You’re not admitting anything. You’re just not doing his debugging anymore. Start there.
Okay. No DM. Just the channel reply tomorrow. I'll start with that and see what happens.

That’s the whole plan. Channel reply, then stop.

Tomorrow: paste the short one, don’t add a preamble, don’t wait to see if he “gets it.” If it skipped the checklist, it doesn’t enter the queue. If staging’s at risk, revert. Same reply if it happens again.

You don’t have to prove you were tired. You just don’t pick up the debug.

You’ve got this.
Alright. No DM. Just the channel reply tomorrow. I'll start with that and see what happens.

Yeah. That’s the move.

Tomorrow: short channel reply, no extra speech, then you’re done with that thread until the checklist is actually done.

You don’t have to manage how he takes it. You just don’t pick up the debug.
